title: The pluperfect: what had already happened in Peru

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the pluperfect (*había* + past participle) from B1 Unit 1. It names something that was already finished before another moment in the past. Pizarro's story is full of these "already" moments: a war, a capture, a city founded earlier.

sections.title: Earlier past and later past
rows: Una guerra ya había dividido el imperio.
Los incas nunca habían visto caballos.
*nunca habían visto*: never before that moment.

items.spanish: Cuando Pizarro llegó, una guerra ya había dividido el imperio.
items.english: When Pizarro arrived, a war had already divided the empire.

items.spanish: Los incas nunca habían visto caballos.
items.english: The Incas had never seen horses.

items.spanish: Antes de 1572, los españoles ya habían ejecutado a Atahualpa.
items.english: Before 1572, the Spaniards had already executed Atahualpa.

items.spanish: En 1572, los españoles ya habían fundado Lima.
items.english: By 1572, the Spaniards had already founded Lima.

sections.content: The form is *había* (singular) or *habían* (plural) + a participle that never changes: *había dividido*, *habían visto*. *Ya* (already) and *nunca* (never) often go with it. Put the later event in the preterite (*llegó*, *capturaron*).
